subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finovate.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the next steps so your team has a single reference.

Pain points (what you told us):
- Unit economics pressure: MLP team is seeing per-API-call costs ~3x higher than budget for peak workloads.
- High variance in sequence length causing unexpected token costs and latency spikes.
- Current infra: in-house Kubernetes serving with a mix of FP16 and CPU fallbacks; no unified KV cache across services.
- Limited ops bandwidth to tune batching and manage quantized model variants.

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce per-token inference cost by 40% while keeping p99 latency under 300ms for 95% of requests.
- Ability to support mixed sequence lengths with predictable billing & a fallback when GPU capacity is constrained.
- Clear plan for a pilot (5k qps peak, 99k monthly requests) and measurable unit-cost improvements within 30 days of pilot start.

What we recommend (high level):
- Start with a 4-week pilot on Redwood Hosted with quantized model variant + automatic batching and prefix/KV caching enabled for the common prompt-set.
- We’ll provide model profiling and kernel recommendations during week 1 and an autoscaling policy tuned for your traffic shape.
- If pilot meets latency and cost targets, transition to Dedicated nodes or Private deployment based on your security needs.

Open items / questions:
- Are you open to an aggressive quantization profile (int8 / q4) for the pilot, with a canary in prod for quality checks? (you mentioned some concern about hallucinations)
- Who on your side will own the integration work (data/traffic instrumentation + a test route for A/B)?
- Any procurement constraints we should loop in for SOW/PO?

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a short SOW + pricing summary for the pilot (attached).
2) Alex — confirm whether engineering can provide a 1-hour test window next week for a traffic replay (suggest Tue/Wed morning PST).
3) We’ll schedule a profiling call with our Applied ML engineer (Marissa) to lock down quantization and expected cost savings.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-summary.xlsx, SOW-draft.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly here.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finovate.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Ben — appreciated the recap, this is helpful.

Quick answers:
- We’re open to int8/q4 quantization for the pilot as long as we get a short quality baseline test (we'll run a 500-sample eval set).
- Engineering owner: Priya (cc'd in a separate thread) will do the integration; she can carve out a 1-hour window next Wednesday (2026-04-08) at 9:30am PST for the replay.
- Procurement: Please include standard PO terms; we have a 30-day review window but can expedite for pilots under $25k.

Can you confirm expected % cost reduction range (ballpark) if batching + KV caching + int8 quantization are applied? We need a number to present to finance.

Thanks,
Alex

Date: 2026-04-06T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and for lining up Priya.

Ballpark cost reduction expectations:
- Batching + KV/prefix caching: 15-25% (depends on hit rate; if 70%+ cache hit we see closer to 25%).
- Int8 / q4 quantization: additional 25-40% (model-dependent; larger models often see larger gains).
- Combined (batching + caching + int8): plausible range 40-60% on per-token compute cost with conservative estimates around ~45% for typical LLM stacks.

Notes: these are compute-cost estimates and don’t include potential infra savings from Dedicated pricing or committed capacity.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Attach a short pricing summary and SOW draft for the pilot (attached). The pricing summary includes a ballpark cost model for the 30-day pilot and projected per-1k-token savings under different hit-rate scenarios.
- Schedule profiling session with Marissa for Wed 2026-04-08 10:30am PST (Marissa will send calendar invite).

If that all looks good I’ll loop in our procurement lead to align SOW terms to your 30-day review window.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
